reason: The fix and its tests (TC-001, TC-004, TC-005) correctly turn the attachment response into a counted `request_error`, and the sentence sits in the Concurrency bullet: it means no check state carries over, since each check starts its own browser. Chromium already handled a possible download before this PR, because `browser.go` never sets a download behaviour (grep finds no `setDownloadBehavior`). The PR does not add that side effect, and technical.md 'Refactoring' lists it as out of scope. Making the sentence more precise and denying downloads is a hardening follow-up, not a defect of this change.
title: Deny downloads in the Amazon browser and make the technical spec precise about it
todo:
**Problem:** `internal/amazon/browser.go` never sets a download behaviour. With `--headless=new`, an Amazon answer with `Content-Disposition: attachment` (now a `request_error`, issue #186) may still be written to disk (profile or `$HOME/Downloads`) on every such check. `doc/specifications/amazon-human-checks/technical.md:205` says "a failed download leaves nothing for the next check", but no test proves it for the disk.

**Suggested work:**
- When the browser starts (in the launch/target set-up steps of `browserTab`/`BrowserCollector`), call `Browser.setDownloadBehavior{behavior: "deny"}`.
- Extend `TestBrowserNavigation_TC001_*` (`internal/amazon/browser_navigation_test.go`) to assert that no file appears in the profile directory or in a temporary `HOME`'s `Downloads` after the attachment check.
- Reword the sentence in technical.md (section "Success response not opened as a page (issue #186)", Backend, last bullet) to describe the actual guarantee, and move the download behaviour out of "Out of scope".

title: Share the log/stdout capture test helper through amazontest
todo:
**Problem:** Three copies of the same helper capture `log` and `os.Stdout` through a pipe: `captureOutput` (`internal/amazon/browser_test.go:157`), the helper in `internal/service/amazon_browser_profile_test.go:184` and `captureCheckOutput` (`internal/httpapi/amazon_browser_navigation_test.go:128`).

**Suggested work:** In a separate refactoring PR, add an exported `amazontest.CaptureOutput(t *testing.T) func() string` in `internal/amazon/amazontest`. Replace the three copies with it and add no behaviour change.

title: Fold the redundant Amazon-answer check into assertNavigationFailure
todo:
**Problem:** In `internal/amazon/browser_navigation_test.go`, lines 83 (TC-001) and 117 (TC-002) check `got.Result` against `price_not_found`/`success`/`unavailable` before calling `assertNavigationFailure`, which already requires `Result == "request_error"`.
